title: Coral and the Vow
premise: Bram Hartwell's failing café survives on one legacy: a decades-old promise that the Hartwell family bakery will inherit a windfall if a vow is spoken aloud by a certain deadline—a vow Bram has dodged for ten years because saying it means confessing he loves Coral Ashby, his late mentor's daughter and his business rival. When a snowstorm traps Bram and Coral in the café overnight with the contract, the truth spills sideways: she has known about the vow all along and has been quietly buying his debts to force the confession before the deadline expires. Saying the sentence saves the café but risks the friendship, until Coral reveals her own decade-old secret—that she engineered the original vow to give him a reason to choose her—and they claim both the inheritance and each other before the clock runs out.
about_author: Freya Dravenmoor is a former pastry cook who traded early-morning ovens for late-night manuscripts, writing love stories set in kitchens, coastal towns, and the spaces between almost and always. She lives in a drafty seaside house with a sourdough starter older than her career and a firm belief that every good romance deserves a deadline.

chapters.title: Three Payments from Gone
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram opens his struggling café at dawn, counting invoices and dodging a call from the bank. A letter from Hartwell & Ashby Legal arrives, reminding him the family vow expires in thirty days. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine, establishing the ticking clock.

chapters.title: The Sentence He Rehearses
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Flashback to the night ten years ago when Bram's grandmother made him promise to speak his truth aloud to inherit the bakery's trust. He's recited the sentence to his reflection a thousand times and never once to Coral. Emotional beat: tender, aching cowardice.

chapters.title: Ashby's on the Corner
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral opens her sleek patisserie across the square, watching Bram's café with something between rivalry and longing. Her lawyer presses her about 'the acquisition file.' Emotional beat: controlled ambition with a hairline crack of guilt.

chapters.title: Cinnamon and Cold War
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The two rivals collide at the farmers' market, trading barbed compliments over the last crate of blood oranges. Old chemistry flares; both retreat. Emotional beat: playful tension that keeps slipping into something warmer.

chapters.title: The Weather Report
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A historic snowstorm is forecast; the bank call comes—final notice, seven days. Coral's shop floods from a burst pipe, and she has nowhere to run when the roads close. Emotional beat: pressure mounting from every side.

chapters.title: Snowed In
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The storm strands Coral at Bram's café when she comes to deliver a 'business proposal.' Power flickers; they're locked in together with flour, candles, and a decade of unsaid things. Emotional beat: reluctant intimacy under forced proximity.

chapters.title: The Contract on the Counter
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Bram discovers the trust contract in Coral's bag—she's been the anonymous buyer of his debts. Fury first: she's been playing him. Then confusion: why would she spend a fortune to corner him into a vow? Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into vertigo.

chapters.title: What She Bought
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Confrontation by candlelight. Coral refuses to explain, only says, 'Say the sentence, Bram. You've had ten years.' He storms to the kitchen and bakes furiously. Emotional beat: wounded pride wrestling with the suspicion she's right.

chapters.title: Ten Years Ago, Briefly
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Flashback: the night of the vow, Coral overheard Bram's grandmother dictate the terms—and said nothing, because the vow named her. She has waited a decade to be chosen freely, not by contract. Emotional beat: guilt braided with hope.

chapters.title: Flour, Salt, Confession
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Truce at 3 a.m.: they bake bread together like they did as apprentices, hands brushing, guards dropping. Bram almost says it; a power outage and a phone call from Coral's lawyer interrupt. Emotional beat: warmth at the edge of confession, snatched away.

chapters.title: Morning After the Storm
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Snowbound streets, one shared breakfast, and the contract still unsigned. Coral leaves before he can speak, leaving a note: 'The deadline is real. So am I.' Emotional beat: hangover of intimacy and the terror of permanence.

chapters.title: The Lawyer's Letter
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram meets the estate lawyer, learning the trust's full terms: if the vow goes unspoken by month's end, the inheritance—and his café—goes to Ashby's Patisserie. Coral knew. Or did she? Emotional beat: paranoia rebuilding walls.

chapters.title: Rival Kitchens
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral launches a counter-campaign for the square's holiday festival, and the town picks sides. Her assistant confronts her: 'You bought a man instead of telling him you loved him.' Emotional beat: the cost of control made visible.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram finds his grandmother's recipe box, and inside, letters between her and Coral's late mother—two friends who engineered the vow together, hoping their heirs would finish what they started. Emotional beat: grief softening into understanding.

chapters.title: What the Vow Actually Says
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Reading the full contract, Bram discovers the vow was never about inheritance—it was his grandmother's way of forcing him to stop hiding. The money is incidental; the sentence is the point. Emotional beat: revelation that reframes his cowardice.

chapters.title: Ashby's, After Dark
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram breaks into his own rival's closed shop to leave an apology tart—and finds Coral asleep at her desk surrounded by ten years of unsent letters to him. Emotional beat: heartbreak and tenderness colliding.

chapters.title: The Letters
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral wakes to find Bram reading her letters. Furious, vulnerable, she finally admits she's loved him since they were apprentices and bought his debts out of desperation, not strategy. Emotional beat: raw, mutual exposure.

chapters.title: Almost the Sentence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They nearly say everything—lips close, hands shaking—but Bram panics that the vow makes his love a legal technicality, and Coral fears the same. They part angry and aching with two days left. Emotional beat: the cruelest almost.

chapters.title: Deadline Eve
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The bank seizes the café's account; Coral offers to tear up the contract and walk away so his choice can be free. Bram realizes refusing the inheritance might be the truest vow of all. Emotional beat: clarity arriving through loss.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At the town's winter festival, before both shops and half the square, Bram speaks the rehearsed sentence aloud—not to the lawyer, but to Coral: that he has loved her for ten years and chooses her without conditions. Emotional beat: cathartic, public, terrifying release.

chapters.title: Coral's Answer
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral answers with a vow of her own, tearing up the debt papers and revealing the trust was always meant to return to both of them jointly. They sign nothing but a shared recipe card. Emotional beat: triumphant, tender resolution of the loyalty-versus-truth thread.

chapters.title: One Kitchen, Two Names
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POV. Spring: the café and patisserie merge into one shop with a new sign—Hartwell & Ashby. The recipe box sits on the counter, and Bram finally stops rehearsing sentences he doesn't need. Emotional beat: earned peace, inheritance redefined as love freely chosen.
